3DFace.description: Draws a single mesh face by picking three or four corner points. Handy for patching an individual hole in a mesh or building simple mesh geometry point by point, much like the old AutoCAD workflow.

3View.description: Splits the screen into a three-viewport arrangement instead of the usual four. Useful when you want a large perspective view alongside a couple of orthographic views without the clutter of a full grid.

About.description: Opens the About Rhino dialog showing the exact version, service release and licence details. Reach for it when reporting a bug or checking whether you are on the latest service release.

AcadSchemes.description: Manages the export schemes used when saving to AutoCAD formats (DWG/DXF). Set up a scheme once — how curves, layers and hatches translate — then reuse it every time you issue drawings to consultants.

AddGuide.description: Places an infinite construction guide line that object snaps recognise but that never prints or exports. Ideal for setting out temporary alignment lines while modelling, without polluting the file with real geometry.

AddMissingBlockAttributeKeys.description: Brings block instances up to date so they all carry the full set of attribute keys defined for the block, adding any that are missing. Useful housekeeping when a block definition has gained new data fields after instances were placed.

AddNextU.description: Grows the current control-point selection by one point in the surface's U direction. Part of the family of selection helpers that make it quick to grab rows of control points for shaping surfaces.

AddNextV.description: Grows the current control-point selection by one point in the surface's V direction. Used with the other row-selection helpers when sculpting surfaces via their control points.

AddPrevU.description: Extends the current control-point selection by one point in the opposite U direction. A quick way to walk a selection along a surface row while fine-tuning form.

AddPrevV.description: Extends the current control-point selection by one point in the opposite V direction. Companion to AddNextV for stepping a selection along a surface column.

AddNgonsToMesh.description: Groups coplanar triangles and quads in a mesh into larger n-sided faces (ngons), giving a cleaner-looking mesh without changing its shape. Useful before exporting to software that prefers ngon meshes, or simply to tidy the wireframe display.

AddObjectsToBlock.description: Adds selected geometry to an existing block definition, updating every instance of that block in the model. Saves redefining a block from scratch when a component design gains an extra part.

Alerter.description: Plays a notification sound when a long-running operation finishes, so you can get on with something else while Rhino churns through a heavy calculation or render mesh. Configure the delay threshold and sound to taste.

AlignVertices.description: Snaps mesh or SubD vertices that sit within a tolerance of each other onto the same location, so nearly-touching edges can then be welded or joined cleanly. A standard first step when repairing meshes with hairline gaps.

ApplyBoxMapping.description: Wraps a texture onto an object by projecting it from the six sides of a box. The go-to mapping for orthogonal, building-like forms where you want materials such as brick or timber to read correctly on every face.

ApplyCrv.description: Takes flat curves drawn in the world XY plane and wraps them onto a target surface using the surface's UV parameterisation. Designers use it to lay out patterns, engraving or panel lines flat, then transfer them onto a curved form.

ApplyCustomMapping.description: Assigns a custom texture-mapping channel to an object, using another object or a custom widget to control how the texture flows across it. For the cases where the standard planar, box, cylindrical and spherical projections cannot follow the form.

ApplyCylindricalMapping.description: Projects a texture onto an object from a surrounding cylinder — the natural choice for columns, tubes, bottles and other rotationally shaped objects where a planar projection would smear.

ApplyMesh.description: Deforms a mesh drawn flat in the XY plane onto a target surface via the surface's UV space — the mesh equivalent of ApplyCrv. Useful for wrapping panelisation or relief patterns onto doubly curved surfaces.

ApplyMeshUVN.description: Wraps a flat mesh onto a surface using UVN coordinates, where the mesh's height above the flat plane becomes an offset along the surface normal. This lets a flat relief pattern gain genuine depth when transferred to a curved surface.

ApplyPlanarMapping.description: Projects a texture flat onto an object from a single plane. The simplest mapping type — right for facades, floors and other broadly flat geometry where you want direct control of texture direction and scale.

ApplySphericalMapping.description: Wraps a texture around an object from an enclosing sphere. Suits domes, globes and rounded forms where cylindrical or planar projections would distort at the poles of the shape.

ApplySurfaceMapping.description: Uses a separate surface as the mapping object, so the texture follows that surface's UV flow rather than a simple projection. Powerful when you need a texture to track a sweeping, doubly curved form precisely.

AreaMoments.description: Calculates area moments of inertia, centroid and related section properties for closed planar curves, hatches or surfaces. Structural-minded designers use it to check section stiffness properties of a profile before handing it to an engineer.

ArrayHolePolar.description: Takes an existing hole in a planar surface and repeats it in a circular pattern around a centre point. Quicker than re-cutting: think bolt circles, perforated discs or radial ventilation patterns.

Arrowhead.description: Adds or removes an arrowhead at the end of a curve, turning plain curves into leader-like graphic arrows. Handy for annotating diagrams and presentation drawings without building full leader annotations.

AttachGHSData.description: Attaches GHS (General HydroStatics) metadata to geometry so hull and compartment models can be exported for naval-architecture stability analysis. Specialist marine tooling — most designers will never need it.

Audit3dmFile.description: Reads a 3dm file from disk and reports its internal structure, tables and any damage, without fully opening it. The first diagnostic to run on a file that refuses to open or behaves strangely.

AutoAlignCPlane.description: Toggles automatic construction-plane alignment, so the CPlane snaps itself to the surface or object under your cursor as you work. Speeds up modelling on angled faces without constantly running CPlane commands by hand.

Autosave.description: Saves the current model to Rhino's autosave file immediately, on demand. A belt-and-braces save before attempting something risky, separate from your named file on disk.

BackgroundBitmap.description: Places, scales and manages a reference image behind the geometry in a single viewport — the traditional way to trace over a scanned sketch, plan or photograph. Largely superseded by Picture objects, but still useful for per-viewport tracing.

Bake.description: Converts procedural textures on an object's material into ordinary bitmap textures. Run it before exporting to software that cannot evaluate Rhino's procedural noise, gradient or tile textures.

BatchRenderNamedViews.description: Renders every (or a chosen set of) named views one after another and saves the images to disk. Set up your camera angles as named views, start the batch, and come back to a full set of presentation renders.

Boss.description: Extrudes closed planar profile curves up to a surface on a solid and unions the result, creating a raised boss feature in one step. A quick way to add pads and protrusions to a part without manual extrusion and boolean work.

Bounce.description: Fires a ray from a start point and direction, reflecting it off surfaces a set number of times to produce a polyline of the bounce path. Useful for quick acoustic or daylight reflection studies inside a space.

BoxEdit.description: Opens a panel for numerically transforming objects via their bounding box — exact position, size and rotation typed in rather than dragged. Invaluable when objects must be a precise overall dimension or sit at exact coordinates.

BringForward.description: Moves a curve, hatch or other 2D element one step up in the draw order, so it displays in front of the object it was behind. Part of the draw-order tools used to compose layered 2D drawings.

BringToFront.description: Puts the selected curves, hatches or annotations at the very top of the draw order so they display in front of everything else. Essential when composing 2D drawings where hatches keep hiding your linework.

BringViewportToTop.description: Makes a named viewport the active, frontmost one — mostly useful in scripts and button macros that need to guarantee which viewport subsequent commands act on.

Calc.description: Pops up an on-screen calculator whose result can be fed straight into the command line. Saves reaching for a separate calculator when a dimension needs working out mid-command.

CalcRPN.description: Opens a Reverse Polish Notation calculator, for those who prefer HP-style stack entry, with results usable directly in the command line. Same job as Calc, different keystroke philosophy.

Cancel.description: Cancels the running command, exactly like pressing Escape. Exists mainly so button macros and scripts can bail out of whatever state Rhino is in before starting fresh.

Catenary.description: Draws a true catenary — the curve a chain takes hanging under its own weight — between two points, with control over length or sag. A gift for architects working on hanging chains, arches, tents and gridshell form-finding sketches.

ChangeSpace.description: Moves objects between model space and a layout's paper space (or between layouts), converting their geometry to suit the destination. Useful when notes or drawing graphics were made in the wrong space.

ChangeToCurrentLayer.description: Moves the selected objects onto whichever layer is current. One of the fastest layer-tidying moves: set the layer you want, select strays, run the command.

CheckInLicense.description: Returns a checked-out Rhino licence to the team's licence server (Zoo or Cloud Zoo) so someone else can use it. Pair of CheckOutLicense for laptop users who roam between office and site.

CheckOutLicense.description: Borrows a licence from the team's licence server so Rhino keeps working while you are offline — on site, on a plane, at home. Check it back in when you return so colleagues aren't locked out.

CheckNewObjects.description: Toggles automatic checking of every newly created or imported object for geometry errors, warning the moment a bad object appears. Slower, but invaluable for tracing exactly which operation is producing invalid geometry.

Clash.description: Runs clash detection between two sets of objects, reporting where they intersect or come within a given clearance. Architects use it to check services against structure, or a design against a site constraint envelope.

ClearAllMeshes.description: Deletes the render and analysis meshes cached in the file for all surfaces and solids, often shrinking the file dramatically before saving or sending. The meshes regenerate automatically next time a shaded view needs them.

ClearAllObjectDisplayModes.description: Removes every per-object display-mode override in the model, returning all objects to the viewport's own display mode. The quick undo for a model peppered with SetObjectDisplayMode experiments.

ClearAnalysisMeshes.description: Deletes the extra-fine meshes created for curvature, draft-angle and similar visual analyses. Frees memory and file size once you have finished analysing.

ClearDrawOrder.description: Resets the draw order of selected 2D elements back to the default, discarding any BringToFront and SendToBack arrangements. Use it when a drawing's stacking has become impossible to reason about.

ClearUndo.description: Empties the undo buffer, releasing the memory it holds. Worth running after huge operations on big models when Rhino is getting sluggish — but be certain you no longer need to undo anything.

CloseRenderWindow.description: Closes the render window. Exists mostly so scripts and batch workflows can tidy up after saving a render.

ClosestPt.description: Finds and marks the closest point on an object from a test point, or the closest points between objects. Useful for measuring minimum clearances and for locating exact contact points before dimensioning.

CloseViewport.description: Closes the active viewport, removing it from the layout of views. Used with NewViewport and floating viewports to customise the workspace.

CollapseMeshEdge.description: Collapses a mesh edge to a single vertex, merging its two end vertices and removing the faces that depended on it. A precise, surgical tool for reducing or repairing meshes one edge at a time.

CollapseMeshFace.description: Collapses a whole mesh face down to a single vertex, welding its corners together. Useful for eliminating awkward slivers and pinch points during manual mesh repair.

CollapseMeshFacesByArea.description: Collapses every mesh face whose area falls below (or within) a threshold you set, removing insignificant faces in one pass. A batch clean-up for scan data and imported meshes littered with tiny faces.

CollapseMeshFacesByAspectRatio.description: Collapses mesh faces whose aspect ratio exceeds a threshold — the long, thin slivers that cause shading artefacts and break downstream tools. Batch companion to the one-at-a-time collapse commands.

CollapseMeshFacesByEdgeLength.description: Collapses mesh faces that have edges shorter (or longer) than a length you specify. Another of the criteria-based batch tools for thinning out problem faces in heavy or messy meshes.

CollapseMeshVertex.description: Merges a chosen mesh vertex into an adjacent one, removing the edge between them. The finest-grained of the collapse tools for hand-editing mesh topology.

CommandHelp.description: Opens the help panel showing documentation for whichever command is running or last ran, updating as you work. Keep it docked while learning and Rhino effectively narrates itself.

CommandList.description: Displays a browsable list of every command available in this Rhino installation, including those added by plug-ins. A good way to discover tools you did not know existed.

CommandPrompt.description: Controls where the command prompt lives — shown, hidden, docked top or bottom, or floating. Purely a workspace preference, but a vital one to know when the prompt vanishes.

ComputeVertexColors.description: Evaluates the texture applied to a mesh and stores the resulting colours directly on the mesh's vertices. Used to carry colour into formats and workflows (3D printing, some viewers) that support vertex colour but not textures.

ConnectSrf.description: Extends and/or trims two surfaces so their edges meet cleanly along a shared boundary — the surface counterpart of Connect for curves. Saves the extend-intersect-trim dance when squaring up construction surfaces.

ContinueCurve.description: Picks up an existing control-point curve at its end and lets you keep placing control points as if you had never stopped. Better than drawing a new curve and joining, because the result stays one smooth curve.

ContinueInterpCrv.description: Continues an existing interpolated curve by adding further through-points from its end. The interpolated-curve twin of ContinueCurve, keeping the extended result a single clean curve.

Convert.description: Rebuilds curves as sequences of lines and arcs (or polylines) within a tolerance. Essential preparation for CNC cutting, laser profiles and export to software that only understands arcs and lines.

ConvertDots.description: Turns annotation dots into text objects or point objects (and can carry the dot text across). Useful when survey or coordination data arrives as dots but you need editable text or plain points.

ConvertExtrusion.description: Converts lightweight extrusion objects into ordinary surfaces and polysurfaces so their full editing toolset becomes available. Run it when a command refuses to work on what looks like a normal box or cylinder.

ConvertTextToBlockAttribute.description: Converts a text object inside a block into an attribute, so each instance of the block can display its own value — think room tags, door numbers, titleblock fields. Key to building data-aware blocks.

ConvertToBeziers.description: Splits curves and surfaces into their constituent single-span Bezier pieces. Occasionally needed for export to systems that only accept Bezier geometry, or for low-level surface analysis.

CopyCPlaneSettingsToAll.description: Copies the active viewport's construction-plane settings — grid spacing, snap, extents — to every other viewport. Keeps the workspace consistent after tuning one viewport's grid.

CopyCPlaneToAll.description: Applies the active viewport's construction plane to all viewports at once. Useful when working on an angled datum — set the CPlane once, and every view shares it.

CopyDetailToViewport.description: Copies the camera and view settings of a layout detail into a model-space viewport, so you can model from exactly the view a drawing shows. The reverse of CopyViewportToDetail.

CopyHole.description: Copies an existing hole in a planar surface to new locations on the same or another planar face. Much faster than re-drawing profiles and re-cutting when a fixing pattern repeats.

CopyLayout.description: Duplicates an entire layout page, including its details and title-block graphics. The quickest way to build a drawing set where every sheet shares the same setup.

CopyRenderWindowToClipboard.description: Copies the current render window image to the system clipboard, ready to paste into an email, document or image editor. Handy for quick design-review snapshots without saving files.

CopyToLayer.description: Copies the selected objects onto another layer, leaving the originals where they are. Ideal for creating option studies or a frozen record copy while continuing to work on the live version.

CopyViewportToDetail.description: Creates a layout detail whose camera matches the current model-space viewport. Set up the perfect view while modelling, then drop it straight onto a sheet.

CreaseSplitting.description: Toggles whether Rhino splits surfaces at kinks (creases) as they are created, or leaves them as single creased surfaces. Advanced modellers switch it off for specific workflows, but split-at-crease is the safer default.

CreateUniqueBlock.description: Turns the selected block instance into a new, independent block definition, so edits to it no longer affect its siblings. The escape hatch when one repeated element needs to diverge from the rest.

Crv2View.description: Builds a 3D curve from two planar curves drawn in different views, combining the shape seen in one view with the shape seen in the other. Classic technique for modelling handles, hulls and rails defined by plan and elevation profiles.

CrvEnd.description: Places a point object at the end of each selected curve. Useful for marking connection points, checking curve direction, or generating snap targets for later operations.

CrvStart.description: Places a point object at the start of each selected curve. A quick visual check of which way curves run — important before lofting, sweeping or flow operations.

CSec.description: Creates cross-section profile curves through a set of shape curves, cutting them with a plane you position. Traditional boat- and product-modelling workflow: define a form with a few character curves, then generate the sections to loft through.

CullControlPolygon.description: Toggles culling of control points and control polygons that face away from the view, so you only see and select the ones on your side of the object. A sanity-saver when point-editing dense surfaces and SubDs.

CullDegenerateMeshFaces.description: Finds and deletes degenerate mesh faces — zero-area slivers whose corners are collinear or coincident. One of the standard passes when repairing imported or scanned meshes for printing or rendering.

Curvature.description: Evaluates curvature at a picked point on a curve or surface, reporting the value and optionally placing the osculating circle. The precise, numeric complement to the visual curvature-graph and false-colour analyses.

CurvatureAnalysisOff.description: Turns off the false-colour curvature analysis display for the selected (or all) objects. Companion switch to CurvatureAnalysis; also exists so macros can end an analysis session cleanly.

CurvatureGraphOff.description: Removes the curvature-graph display from the selected (or all) curves and surfaces. The off-switch for CurvatureGraph once you have finished checking fairness.

CurveThroughPolyline.description: Fits a smooth NURBS curve through (or controlled by) the vertices of a polyline. The quick route from a faceted survey or GIS polyline to a clean, fair curve.

CurveThroughSrfControlPt.description: Creates curves that pass through a surface's rows or columns of control points. Useful for extracting the underlying structure of a surface to rebuild, analyse or re-loft it.

DeleteFaces.description: Deletes selected sub-object faces from a polysurface, SubD or mesh, leaving the remainder open. Faster than extracting then deleting when you simply want faces gone — say, removing a glazing face to model into an opening.

DeleteMeshNgons.description: Removes ngon groupings from a mesh, returning it to plain triangles and quads without moving any vertices. The undo for AddNgonsToMesh when downstream software chokes on ngons.

DeleteSubCrv.description: Removes the portion of a curve between two points you pick, leaving the rest intact. Cleaner than splitting and deleting when you just need a gap in a curve.

DevLoft.description: Creates a developable surface between two rail curves — one that can be unrolled perfectly flat without stretching. Fundamental for sheet-metal, plywood and fabric construction where material cannot deform in-plane.

Diameter.description: Reports the diameter of curvature at a picked point on a curve — twice the radius the curve is bending through there. Quick check of whether an arc or curve meets a minimum bend diameter.

DigBeep.description: Toggles the confirmation beep a connected 3D digitising arm makes when a point is taken. Small quality-of-life setting for long digitising sessions.

DigCalibrate.description: Re-establishes the relationship between a connected digitising arm's coordinate system and the Rhino model, by taking reference points. Run it whenever the physical object or arm has moved.

DigDisconnect.description: Disconnects the currently connected 3D digitising arm from Rhino. Housekeeping command at the end of a digitising session.

Digitize.description: Connects a 3D digitising arm (MicroScribe, Faro and similar) so its stylus can feed real-world points straight into Rhino commands. The entry point for reverse-engineering physical objects by touch.

DigLine.description: Draws line segments from points taken with a connected digitising arm. One of the sketching commands available while a digitizer is driving input.

DigPause.description: Temporarily suspends digitizer input so you can use the mouse and keyboard normally, then resume taking points. Practical mid-session control during long digitising work.

DigScale.description: Sets a scale factor between the physical object under the digitising arm and the Rhino model, so you can digitise a scale model and receive full-size geometry (or vice versa).

DigSection.description: Traces section curves across a physical object using a digitising arm, producing planar profile curves in the model. A staple of hands-on reverse engineering before lofting surfaces through the sections.

DigSketch.description: Sketches freehand curves by dragging the stylus of a connected digitising arm across a physical surface. The digitizer equivalent of the Sketch command.

DimArea.description: Places an annotation reporting the area of a closed curve, hatch or surface, and keeps it linked so it updates when the geometry changes. Perfect for room areas and site-area schedules on drawings.

DimRecenterText.description: Snaps dimension text that has been dragged around back to its default position on the dimension line. Fast tidy-up for drawings where text has wandered during editing.

DimVolume.description: Places an annotation reporting the volume of closed solids, linked so it updates as the model changes. Useful for quick cut-and-fill notes, tank capacities or massing figures directly on a drawing.

DisableClippingPlane.description: Switches off selected clipping planes in chosen viewports without deleting them, restoring the uncut view. Toggle sections on and off as you flip between design work and section checking.

DisableOsnap.description: Temporarily disables all persistent object snaps (or re-enables them), like clicking Disable on the osnap toolbar. Mostly used in macros, or when snaps keep grabbing unwanted points during freehand work.

DisplayCommandPrompt.description: Shows or hides the command prompt window. The rescue command to type blind when the prompt has disappeared and Rhino seems unresponsive to instructions.

DisplayProperties.description: Opens the display panel for the active viewport, exposing the current display mode's settings for quick adjustment. Faster than digging through Options when you just want to tweak shadows, edges or background.

DocumentPropertiesPage.description: Opens the Document Properties dialog directly at a named page — units, grid, mesh settings and so on. Chiefly a scripting and toolbar-button convenience for jumping straight to a settings page.

DocumentText.description: Manages document user text — named key/value pairs stored in the file itself, such as project number, revision or client. These fields can drive titleblock text, making them the backbone of consistent drawing sets.

DollyZoom.description: Zooms by moving the camera forwards or backwards while simultaneously changing the lens length, keeping the target framed — the cinematic 'vertigo' effect. Useful for tuning perspective drama in a view without losing composition.

Domain.description: Reports the parameter domain of a curve or surface — the internal number range over which it is defined. A geometry-nerd utility that matters when scripting or diagnosing parameterisation issues.

Dot.description: Places an annotation dot — a small text tag that always faces the camera and stays the same size on screen at any zoom. The go-to markup for labelling, redlining and to-do notes inside a model.

DownloadLibraryTextures.description: Fetches the full-resolution textures for Rhino's built-in material library that are not shipped with the installer. Run it once on a new machine so library materials render properly.

DraftAngleAnalysisOff.description: Turns off the false-colour draft-angle analysis display. The off-switch once you have finished checking pull directions for moulding, casting or formwork.

DragMode.description: Sets how objects and control points move when dragged with the mouse — along the construction plane, in world axes, along surface UVN directions, or following the control polygon. Switching drag mode is key to sculpting surfaces and SubDs predictably.

DragStrength.description: Scales how far objects and control points actually move relative to your mouse drag, from full strength down to fine fractions. Turn it down for delicate control-point sculpting where full-strength drags are too coarse.

DrapePt.description: Drops a rectangular grid of points onto whatever geometry lies below, like draping in points rather than a surface. Useful for sampling terrain or scan data at a regular spacing.

DupAnnotationStyle.description: Duplicates an existing annotation (dimension) style as the starting point for a new one. Standard practice for building a family of related drawing styles — copy the office standard, tweak the scale or arrows.

DupLayer.description: Duplicates a layer, optionally including all the objects on it. Quick way to spin off a design option or archive the current state of one layer before major edits.

DupMeshEdge.description: Creates curves that duplicate selected mesh edges. Handy for extracting construction lines from a mesh — a ridge line, a panel joint — to rebuild as clean NURBS geometry.

DupMeshHoleBoundary.description: Creates closed polylines around the holes in a mesh. The first step in patching: extract the hole boundaries, then use them to build filling geometry or to see where a scan is incomplete.

EarthAnchorPoint.description: Assigns a real-world latitude, longitude and north direction to a point in the model, geolocating it on the planet. Prerequisite for accurate sun studies and for exports that carry geographic position.

EditLightByHighlight.description: Repositions a light by clicking where you want its highlight to fall on a surface; Rhino moves the light to produce that reflection. An intuitive way to art-direct speculars in product-style renders.

EditLightByLooking.description: Aims a light by letting you navigate a viewport as if looking through the light itself — where you point the view is where the light points. The quickest way to aim spotlights precisely at what matters.

EditPythonScript.description: Opens Rhino's built-in Python script editor with debugging, so you can write and run Python automation against the live document. The doorway into scripting for anyone automating repetitive modelling or data tasks.

EditScript.description: Opens the RhinoScript editor for writing and debugging scripts in Rhino's classic VBScript-based language. Legacy alongside Python, but plenty of office automation still runs on it.

EMapOff.description: Turns off the environment-map (chrome-ball style) analysis display and returns objects to normal shading. The off-switch after checking surface fairness with EMap reflections.

EnableClippingPlane.description: Re-activates clipping planes in chosen viewports so they cut the model again. Pairs with DisableClippingPlane for flicking section cuts on and off while you work.

Enter.description: Acts exactly like pressing the Enter key. Exists so toolbar buttons and macros can confirm defaults or repeat the previous command without keyboard input.

EnterEnd.description: Sends Enter repeatedly until the current command has completely finished, however many nested prompts remain. A macro-writer's tool for guaranteeing a clean state before the next instruction.

Environments.description: Opens the Environments panel where rendering environments — HDRI backdrops, skylight sources, reflection settings — are created and assigned. Central to getting believable lighting in rendered views.

EvaluateUVPt.description: Reports the U and V parameter values at a picked location on a surface. A niche but occasionally vital utility when scripting, texture-mapping or diagnosing surface parameterisation.

Exit.description: Closes Rhino, prompting to save any unsaved changes first. The command-line equivalent of quitting from the File menu.

ExplodeBlock.description: Replaces block instances with copies of their component geometry, including bursting nested blocks in one go. Use it deliberately — you gain editability but lose the block link that kept instances coordinated.

ExportBitmaps.description: Saves the bitmap textures embedded in the current file out to a folder on disk. Essential when a model arrives with packed textures and you need the images for editing or for another application.

ExportBlockAttributes.description: Writes the attribute data carried by block instances out to a spreadsheet-friendly file. This is how door schedules, fixture counts and similar tabulations get from a block-based model into Excel.

ExportRuiFile.description: Saves toolbar and interface customisations to an RUI file that can be backed up or shared. How an office distributes its standard toolbar setup across workstations.

ExtendCrvOnSrf.description: Extends a curve that lies on a surface along its natural path until it reaches the surface edges. Perfect for completing trim curves and panel lines that stop short of the boundary.

ExtendDynamic.description: Extends a curve by dragging its endpoint to wherever you want it, with the extension following the curve smoothly. The freehand cousin of Extend for when you don't have a boundary to extend to.

ExtractAnalysisMesh.description: Pulls out the fine mesh Rhino built for a visual analysis (curvature, draft angle, zebra) as a real mesh object you can keep. Useful when you want that high-quality mesh for export or further processing.

ExtractConnectedMeshFaces.description: Selects and extracts all mesh faces connected to a picked face, optionally stopping at edges sharper than a given angle. Great for splitting a scan into logical regions — a roof plane, a wall face — along its natural creases.

ExtractControlPolygon.description: Creates a polyline (for curves) or mesh (for surfaces) that duplicates the control polygon — the straight-line cage joining the control points. Useful for analysing structure or reusing the cage as construction geometry.

ExtractCurvatureGraph.description: Converts the on-screen curvature-graph display into actual curve objects. Lets you keep, print or dimension the curvature 'porcupine' as documentary evidence of a curve's fairness.

ExtractDuplicateMeshFaces.description: Finds faces that exist twice in a mesh — a common flaw in imported and merged meshes — and pulls the duplicates out as a separate mesh for inspection or deletion. Duplicate faces break 3D printing and boolean operations, so this is a standard repair pass.

ExtractMeshFacesByArea.description: Separates mesh faces whose area falls within a range you specify into their own mesh. A diagnostic and repair filter for isolating suspiciously tiny (or huge) faces in scan data.

ExtractMeshFacesByAspectRatio.description: Separates mesh faces whose aspect ratio exceeds a threshold — the long thin slivers — into their own mesh. Isolate them, inspect them, then repair or delete without touching the healthy faces.

ExtractMeshFacesByDraftAngle.description: Separates mesh faces whose slope relative to a pull direction falls within a chosen range. Useful far beyond moulding: pull all roof planes from a terrain scan, or every overhanging face from a print check.

ExtractMeshFacesByEdgeLength.description: Separates mesh faces containing edges shorter or longer than limits you set into their own mesh. Another of the criteria filters for hunting down problem geometry inside big meshes.

ExtractNonManifoldMeshEdges.description: Finds edges shared by more than two faces — non-manifold junctions that make a mesh unprintable and unbooleanable — and extracts the offending faces for repair. A core step in preparing meshes for 3D printing.

ExtractPt.description: Creates point objects at the control points, edit points or vertices of the selected geometry. Useful for rebuilding geometry from its defining points, or exporting point sets to other software.

ExtractRenderMesh.description: Copies the display mesh Rhino generated for a surface or solid out as an editable mesh object. The standard way to get a mesh that matches exactly what you see shaded on screen — often as a starting point for export or mesh editing.

ExtractSubCrv.description: Copies (or removes) the portion of a curve between two picked points as a separate curve. Cleaner than split-and-delete when you need just one segment of a longer curve.

ExtractUVMesh.description: Creates a flat mesh laid out in a surface's UV parameter space. Paired with ApplyMesh or ApplyMeshUVN, it forms a round-trip workflow: flatten, design in 2D, wrap the result back onto the 3D surface.

ExtrudeMesh.description: Extrudes mesh faces or whole meshes in a straight line, creating new connected mesh volume. The mesh-world equivalent of extruding surfaces — often used to give thickness to open scan patches.

ExtrudeSrfAlongCrv.description: Sweeps a surface along a path curve, producing the solid it traces out. Useful for creating swept solids where a profile face must travel a curved route — a moulded string, a curved wall from its section.

ExtrudeSrfToPoint.description: Extrudes a surface so it tapers to a single apex point, producing a pyramid- or cone-like solid from any face. Handy for spires, funnels and quick massing of pitched forms.

ExtrudeSubD.description: Extrudes SubD faces or edges outwards, adding connected new faces while keeping everything a single smooth SubD. One of the fundamental moves of SubD box-modelling — grow limbs, fins and volumes straight out of the form.

Fin.description: Extrudes a curve lying on a surface along the surface's normals (or at an angle to them), creating a fin-like surface that stands off the base. Ideal for ribs, brims, flanges and stiffeners that must follow a curved parent surface.

FindText.description: Searches the model for text objects, dots, leaders and annotations containing a given string, and can zoom to and select the matches. Lifesaver on large drawing files when you need to find every instance of a room name or note.

FitSrf.description: Refits a surface to a specified tolerance, adjusting its control-point structure — often dramatically simplifying over-dense surfaces. Use it to lighten heavy imported surfaces while keeping shape deviation within tolerance.

FixedLengthCrvEdit.description: Lets you drag and reshape a curve while Rhino preserves its overall length exactly. Invaluable when the curve represents something physically inextensible — a cable, chain, strip of material — that must keep its length as it moves.

FlatShade.description: Toggles flat shading in the viewport, rendering each mesh facet as a hard plane instead of smoothing across them. Reveals the true underlying render mesh — useful for judging mesh density and diagnosing shading artefacts.

FlattenSrf.description: Produces a flat, planar version of a surface based on its untrimmed UV structure, keeping the trim curves in place on the flat copy. Combined with ApplyCrv and ApplyMesh, it underpins flatten–design–rewrap workflows for decorating curved surfaces.

GCon.description: Reports the geometric continuity — G0 position, G1 tangency, G2 curvature — between the ends of two curves. The objective test when you need to know whether two curves genuinely flow into one another.

GetDocumentUserText.description: Reads and reports the document user text stored in the file — the named key/value pairs such as project number or revision. Chiefly useful in scripts and macros that need those values.

GetUserText.description: Reads and reports the user text attached to selected objects — per-object key/value data such as part numbers or specifications. The retrieval half of Rhino's simple object-data system, alongside SetUserText.

GlobalEdgeContinuity.description: Displays continuity analysis across the matched edges of a model at once, rather than one edge pair at a time. Lets surface modellers audit an entire patch layout for position, tangency and curvature quality in a single view.

GradientView.description: Toggles a graduated background in the viewport in place of the flat background colour. Purely cosmetic, but a two-tone backdrop instantly makes screenshots and client-facing views feel more finished.

GrasshopperDeveloperSettings.description: Opens Grasshopper's developer settings, controlling assembly folders and how add-on libraries are loaded. Strictly for people writing or debugging Grasshopper components.

GrasshopperFolders.description: Opens Grasshopper's special folders — Libraries, UserObjects and friends — directly in the file explorer. The quick route to installing a downloaded plug-in or backing up custom clusters.

GrasshopperGetSDKDocumentation.description: Retrieves the Grasshopper SDK documentation for component developers. Only relevant if you are programming your own Grasshopper components.

GrasshopperLoadOneByOne.description: Loads Grasshopper add-on libraries one at a time with a prompt between each, so a crashing or misbehaving plug-in can be identified by elimination. The classic troubleshooting mode when Grasshopper will not start cleanly.

GrasshopperPluginList.description: Reports the Grasshopper add-on libraries present in this installation. Useful for auditing what is loaded when diagnosing conflicts or documenting a workstation setup.

GroundPlane.description: Controls the infinite ground plane used in rendered and raytraced views — its height, material and whether it only catches shadows. The fastest way to ground a model so renders stop floating in space.

GumballAlignment.description: Sets which frame the gumball widget aligns to — the construction plane, the object itself, or world axes. Switching alignment is the difference between dragging a rotated panel along its own edge and along the world grid.

GumballAutoReset.description: Toggles whether a manually relocated gumball snaps back to its default position after each use, or stays where you put it. A workflow preference for heavy gumball users who repeatedly transform about a custom pivot.

GumballRelocate.description: Moves and reorients the gumball widget itself without moving the selected objects, setting a custom pivot and axes for the next transformation. Essential for rotating or scaling about a specific corner, edge or datum rather than the selection's centre.

GumballReset.description: Returns the gumball widget to its default position, orientation and settings for the current selection. The quick fix after relocating or reorienting the gumball leaves it somewhere unhelpful.

GumballScaleMode.description: Sets how the gumball's scale handles behave — whether dragging one handle scales in that single direction or scales the selection uniformly in all directions. Worth knowing so a quick handle-drag stretches or resizes exactly as intended.
